html:
A free Black merchant born in Virginia who moved to Liberia in 1829, became its governor in 1841 and its first president after independence in 1847.

He served from 1848 to 1856 and again from 1872 to 1876. He travelled to Europe to win recognition from Britain and France, and pushed the borders of the state along the coast through treaties with local rulers. He was the first president of Liberia College. His career shows both sides of the settler republic: freedom for Black Americans, and rule over the native peoples of the interior. Compare Edward Blyden.
